# Anti-pattern catalog

<!-- Generated by scripts/gen_rule_docs.py. Do not edit by hand. -->

[`rules/anti-patterns.yaml`](../../rules/anti-patterns.yaml) and it is the authority;
these pages are generated from it and cannot drift from it.

## How to read a page

| Section | What it is |
|---|---|
| Intent | What the anti-pattern is |
| Detection signals | What the regexes look for, and what they miss |
| Escape hatches | The `none_of` patterns that suppress the rule, and why |
| Known false-positive modes | Where the rule fires on something it should not |
| Synthetic examples | One firing case and one quiet case |
| Corrective action | The `fix` string the tool prints |
| Changelog | When the rule changed and why |

## Two things the generated pages reveal on purpose

1. **The patterns are public.** The catalog is embedded in the binary, so hiding the
   regexes would hide nothing. What is *not* public is any target: no page, pattern or
   example names a program, a chain or a repository.
2. **The pages carry ecosystem tokens; the catalog does not.** A pattern that matches an
   ecosystem's test marker is shown here verbatim, because a rule page that cannot say
   what it matches is useless. The *balanced pack set* in
   [`rules/packs/`](../../rules/packs/) is what keeps that from being a statement
   about the author - see [`docs/tripwires.md`](../tripwires.md).
